title: 〜まみれ
meaning: covered all over in … (mud, sweat, blood, dust)
simpleExplanation: 〜まみれ attaches to a noun and means "covered all over with X", where X is an unpleasant substance that sticks to a surface: 泥まみれ (covered in mud), 汗まみれ (drenched in sweat), 血まみれ (bloodstained). Figuratively, 借金まみれ (drowning in debt).
whenUsed: Both speech and writing, neutral to vivid. Used for physical states after work, sport, accidents and for dirt (ほこりまみれ). Only liquids and fine particles that coat a surface work; for many objects scattered around, use だらけ.
formation: N + まみれ (泥・汗・血・ほこり・油・借金)
N + まみれだ / まみれになる / まみれの + N

examples.ja: 子供たちは泥まみれになって遊んでいた。
examples.reading: こどもたちはどろまみれになってあそんでいた。
examples.en: The children were playing, covered in mud.
examples.note: 泥まみれになって: the mud coats the children.

examples.ja: 彼は汗まみれの顔でゴールに飛び込んだ。
examples.reading: かれはあせまみれのかおでゴールにとびこんだ。
examples.en: He dashed across the finish line, his face covered in sweat.
examples.note: 汗まみれの顔: adnominal use with の.

examples.ja: 会社は借金まみれで、倒産寸前だった。
examples.reading: かいしゃはしゃっきんまみれで、とうさんすんぜんだった。
examples.en: The company was drowning in debt and on the verge of bankruptcy.
examples.note: 借金まみれ: the figurative use for being buried in debt.

examples.ja: 倉庫の棚は、長年放置されてほこりまみれだった。
examples.reading: そうこのたなは、ながねんほうちされてほこりまみれだった。
examples.en: The warehouse shelves, left untouched for years, were covered in dust.
examples.note: ほこり is a fine particle, so まみれ fits.

examples.ja: 整備士は油まみれの手で、笑顔を見せた。
examples.reading: せいびしはあぶらまみれのてで、えがおをみせた。
examples.en: The mechanic smiled with hands covered in oil.
examples.note: 油まみれ: grease coating the hands.

similarGrammar.difference: "Full of" many countable things or faults (傷だらけ・間違いだらけ). まみれ is for a substance coating a surface.
"Entirely of one kind" (黒ずくめ・ごちそうずくめ); not about dirt at all.
"Left as is" (つけっぱなし); sometimes confused because both describe a neglected state.

commonMistakes.why: Mistakes are countable items scattered through the text; use だらけ.
まみれ implies something unpleasant sticking to a surface; flowers do not fit.
Sweat is a liquid that coats the body, so まみれ is the natural choice.

usageNotes: The nouns are limited: 泥・汗・血・ほこり・油・砂・粉, plus figurative 借金・嘘 (rare).
It always suggests dirtiness or exhaustion; there is no positive まみれ.
Grammatically it works like a noun: まみれだ, まみれの, まみれになる.
jlptTips: If the noun is 泥・汗・血・ほこり and the state is dirty or exhausting, choose まみれ.
The main distractor is だらけ; decide by whether the noun is a coating (まみれ) or countable items (だらけ).
ずくめ appears alongside as a third option; it means "nothing but" and is not about dirt.
